messages:
marta: Heads-up: overnight saw a recurring p95 bump when very short requests get merged into long-lived cohorts. Looks like a deadline corridor inversion.
nick: Any quick trace example?
marta: snippet:
[00:12:03] enqueue id=a1 tokens=4 cohort_hint=short
[00:12:03] enqueue id=a2 tokens=6 cohort_hint=short
[00:12:04] merge: src=cohort_9 -> tgt=cohort_1 (age=45s) score=0.81
[00:12:04] dispatch cohort=1 exec_path=kvmix_long p95_inflation=90ms

oliver: So our merge heuristic is too myopic (size + wait). We need age-awareness + variance-aware veto.
priya: Proposal: add two cheap checks at admission: (1) age_penalty: reduce merge_score by lambda*age_seconds, (2) variance_veto: lookup flip_prob from small RMS table keyed by (max/mean ratio, cohort_size). If flip_prob > 0.25 veto merge.
quinn: Also add a micro_token_reserve per-worker to let tiny cohorts survive briefly; if reserve exhausted allow merges (backpressure).
marta: Implementation plan: data job to build flip_prob table (1 day), cohort metrics (mean/max/n/age) in admission store (1 day), admission checks + cooldown TTL for vetoed cohorts (2 days), metrics and canary (2 days).
nick: Metrics: merge_veto_rate, micro_reserve_usage, kernel_flip_rate. Simulation: replay 24h trace sweep for lambda and flip threshold.
priya: Risks: more batches -> ~3-6% cost. Multi-tenant microbursts could deplete reserve; mitigate with per-tenant credits and leaky-bucket refill.
canary-bot: scheduled canary: cohort-guardrails/v0.1 -> canary cluster delta-1 on 2026-04-12T02:00:00Z. Health checks: p95_latency, merge_veto_rate, micro_reserve_exhaustion.
marta: Great. I'll open the data job and a small RFC note. Post sims here when ready.
